item: The custody log follows the post-quantum half of its signing key through rotation records (open-on-main rows 42-44; R716; R717)
key_paths: src/custody/log.py; scripts/verify_custody.py; docs/SECURITY.md; docs/USER_MANUAL.md; tests/test_custody_pqc_rotation.py; tests/test_custody_key_rotation.py; src/api/custody.py; src/ingest/pipeline.py; src/static/app-ai-tools.js; docs/QUICKSTART.md; tests/test_custody_r716_r717.py
summary: Rows 42-44. A change of the ML-DSA half alone (post-quantum signing turned on or off, its key re-created) wrote no key-rotation record, so a pinned check refused the honest log; it now writes one. Turning post-quantum on passes on the Ed25519 key's word; dropping or replacing the ML-DSA half needs the previous identity's endorsement (turning it off gets it from the key still in the folder) or is an unendorsed rotation, since a holder of the Ed25519 key alone could write it (found by both security reads). The checker now follows the ML-DSA key each identity has shown: an entry that drops or replaces it with no record is refused (before any 0.5.1 record it is accepted by name, as post-quantum turned off before 0.5.1 left exactly that), so one entry signed with the Ed25519 key alone cannot launder a forged record (found by the delta read). Every new record names the whole previous identity: its endorsement binds and must carry the previous ML-DSA key, what the entries before it showed and the record before it must agree, it must be signed with the key it introduces, an older record endorsed without the shown ML-DSA key counts as unendorsed, and an old-style record after a new one is refused. Under --pin a head stripped to its Ed25519 half under a signer that names an ML-DSA key is refused. With post-quantum on and its library missing, the log signs nothing (entry owed, 503) instead of writing Ed25519-only entries or a record nobody chose. Older checkers refuse a log with an ML-DSA-only record (fail closed). R716: a check that passes only by accepting an unendorsed key change exits 4 and its VERIFIED line says so (the in-app check shows a warning, never a plain verified); the flag, when it is needed and what it does not prove are in the checker, QUICKSTART, SECURITY and USER_MANUAL. R717: with post-quantum on and the library missing nothing is signed, entries on ingest stay owed and are signed in order once it is back, the routes answer 503, and Settings names the reason and the fix in 12 languages.
